questions.question: The Coriolis Force is caused by __________.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**earth’s rotation**__** . **

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

 
• Coriolis force:

 
 
• ​The rotation of the earth about its axis affects the direction of the wind and this force is called the Coriolis force.
 
• It is directly proportional to the angle of latitude.
 
• It deflects the wind to the left direction in the southern hemisphere and the right direction in the northern hemisphere.
 
• Coriolis force deflects surface currents At an angle of about 45 degrees to the wind-to the right in the Northern Hemisphere, left in the Southern Hemisphere.
 
• It is maximum at the poles and is absent at the equator.
 
• The force acts perpendicular to the pressure gradient force.
 
• The Coriolis force is zero at the equator and the wind blows perpendicular to the isobars.
 
• Major surface ocean currents in the open ocean, however, are set in motion by the wind, which drags on the surface of the water as it blows. The winds pull surface water with them, creating currents. As these currents flow westward, the Coriolis effect, a force that results from the rotation of the Earth, deflects them.
 
 

 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/b5d309a4703fb6ee156ad105ab1a4035194d68085364f2cbfe08fb9b483d4cbf.png] [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f7b7533525eae5e3efa4188d7f04db943960c29a341ef0f6287d86dbaabeb3bf.png] 

 
• **Tidal Waves - **

 
 
• The strongest force responsible for the phenomenon of tides is the Gravitational force of the moon.
 
• The gra vitational pulls between the earth, moon, and sun dictate the tides. The moon, however, influences tides the most.
 
• When two masses are placed at some distance to each other then it applies force on each other. This force is called gravitational force.
 
• Newton’s law of gravitation: According to this law- When two objects having some masses are placed at a certain distance then the gravitational force is directly proportional to the product of masses and it is inversely proportional to the square of the distance between them.
 
• The moon and sun are the main reason for the rising and falling of ocean tides.
 
• As the moon is closer to earth so the gravitational pull of the moon is more than that of the gravitational pull of the sun. So the tidal effect of the moon is more than that of the sun.
 
• Hence the strongest reason for Tidal waves or ocean waves in the sea is the Gravitational effect of the Moon.
 
 
 
• **Wind -**
 
 
• The **wind blows** because of **differences in air pressure** from one location to another.
 
• The **wind blows** from** areas of high pressure** toward** areas of low pressure**. 
 
• If the **high-pressure area** is very close to** the low-pressure area**, or if the** pressure difference** is very great, the** wind** can** blow very fast**.
 
• **Air pressure** depends on the **density of the air**, or how close together its** molecules **are.
 
• **Air lower** in the **atmosphere** is denser than the **air** above, so** air pressure down low is greater than air pressure higher up.**
 
• **Temperature also makes changes in air pressure.**
 
• In **cold air,** the **molecules **are more closely packed together than in **warm air**, so** cold air **is **denser** than **warm air**.
 
• Since** warm air** is less dense and creates less **air pressure**, it** will rise**; **cold air** is denser and creates** greater air pressure**, and so it will **sink**.
 
• When** warm air rises**, **cooler air** will often move in to replace it, so wind often moves from areas where it's colder to areas where it's **warmer.**
 
• The greater the difference between the **high** and **low pressure** or the **shorter** the distance between the high and **low-pressure areas**, the** faster** the **wind will blow**.
 
• **Wind** also** blows** faster if there's nothing in its way, so winds are usually **stronger over oceans** or **flat ground**.
 
• **Meteorologists** can** forecast **the speed and direction of the wind by **measuring air pressure** with a **barometer**.

questions.question: Which of the following physical quantities has same SI unit as that of work?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Energy**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• Work:__

 __
 
• Work is the product of force and displacement. Work transfers energy from one place to another, or one form to another.
 
• The SI unit of work is the joule (J).
 
• Joule is equal to the work done by a force of one Newton acting through one meter.
 
• Dimension Formula for Joule is [M¹L²T⁻²].
 
• 1 Joule = 107 ergs.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• Energy:__

 __
 
• The SI unit of energy is the joule (the symbol for it is J).​
 
 
 
• Power:__
 
 
• It is defined as the work per unit of time.
 
• Its S.I unit of power is Watt.

questions.question: ______ is a popular game in Assam and resembles kabaddi played with a ball.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Dhopkhel**__**.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Kabaddi **is a team sport that is played between two teams with each team comprising 7 players in which a player from one team (referred to as a raider) goes to the opposition's court and touches the opposition players and has to return to their court. 

 
 
• The opposition or called the defence has to hold off the raider and get them out of the court and then the raider is declared out.
 
 
 
• **Dhopkhel is a traditional season game from Assam that is played during the Bihu festival** and is played between two teams with each team of 11 players and the field is bounded by four flags.
 
• **In this game, a rubber ball is thrown into the air by one of the teams and the ball has to be taken by the opposition and if not then that team does not get a chance to throw.**
 
 
• **This game is similar to the Kabaddi game. Hence option 4 is correct.**
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Field Hockey** is a standard Hockey sport that consists of 10 players and a Goalkeeper.

 
 
• ​**Both teams have to hit the ball towards the opponent's court with a hockey stick**** and the goalkeeper has to hold the ball.**
 
 
 
• **Cricket** is a team sport that originated in the UK. The two teams consist of 11 players each with a wicketkeeper.
 
 
• **The team winning the toss can choose either batting or bowling. The team that picks batting has to score runs in the given overs and the team that bats second (or chasing team) has to chase the total.**
 
 
 
• **Kho-Kho** is a team sport with each of the two teams comprising 12 players per side out of them 9 play on the rectangular ground.
 
 
• In this, 9 players from the attacking team are on the field, with eight of them sitting adjacent in the line, while 3 runners from the defending team run around the court and try to avoid being touched.

questions.question: In which year did the Mongols under Genghis Khan invade Transoxiana in North-East Iran?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**1219**__.

__
 
• **Genghis Khan was the founder of the Mongol Empire in 1206 and launched military campaigns in China and Central Asia.**

 
 
• ​The Mongols were a nomadic tribe whole lived between the Ural Mountains and the Gobi Desert in Central Asia who always was at war until their military general, Temujin or also called Genghis Khan united them.
 
 
 
• **The Mongols under Genghis Khan invaded Transoxiana in North-East Iran in 1219. Hence option 1 is correct.**
 
• **Genghis Khan invaded the Jin dynasty in China in 1214 and annexed the Qara Khitai in Central Asia in 1218.**
 
• Mongols attacked India between 1221 and 1327 and later by Qaraunas of Mongol origin.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• Transoxiana is the region located in lower Central Asia and represents modern-day eastern Uzbekistan, Tajikistan in the west, southern parts of Kazakhstan and Turkmenistan. 
 
• **The battle of Indus was fought between Genghis Khan of the Mongol Empire and Jalal ad-Din Mingburnu of the Khwarezmian Empire in 1221 and resulted in the victory of the Mongols.**
 
• In 1227, Ghengis Khan died of illness during his last campaign against Western Xia.

questions.question: Which of the following classifications do humans NOT fall under?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Porifera**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Humans are classified as animals by Carolus Linnaeus (called the father of taxonomy)** and are termed the scientific name homo sapiens in 1758.
 
• Humans are classified based on the groups **Animalia (Kingdom), Chordata (Phylum), Vertebrata (Subphylum), Mammalia (Class), Primates (Order), Hominidae (Superfamily), and Homo (Genus).**
 
• **Porifera are sponges that are invertebrate animals that live in aquatic habitat** and is not one of the human classifications. **Hence option 2 is correct.**
 
 
• These are made of a group of cells that work together for functioning.
 
• They live in marine, and freshwater lakes as well as shallow ocean conditions.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Species with phylum Chordata (animals with a backbone) are vertebrates and humans have a backbone and so they belong to the animal phylum called Chordates.**
 
• Humans resemble apes because of the bodies that are structurally and genetically close to apes and so humans belong to the family Hominidae.
 
 
• **Hominidae refers to the family of humans and extinct or close relatives**.
 
 
 
• **Vertebrata is a subphylum under phylum Chordata** and vertebrates refer to the animals that** have back bone and the skeleton.**

questions.question: Ramabhar Stupa, which marks the site where Lord Buddha was cremated, is situated in which state of India?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Uttar Pradesh**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Lord Buddha was born in the Lumbini, Nepal and is considered the founder of Buddhism.**

 
 
• He was also called Sakyamuni because he belongs to the Sakya clan.
 
 
 
• At the age of 35, **Gautama buddha or Siddhartha got enlightenment in Bodh Gaya** under the Bodhi tree on Vishaka Purnima.
 
• **He gave his first sermon at Sarnath in Uttat Pradesh.**
 
• In 487 BC, Buddha had reached Kushinagar and attained Parinirvana and due to illness, he died in Kushinagar.
 
 
• **His body was cremated at Ramabhar Stupa, Kushinagar, Uttar Pradesh. Hence option 4 is correct. **
 
• **This is called Mahaparinirvana** which is one of the goals of Buddhism and Buddhist text Mahaparinibbana Sutta mentions the death of Lord Buddha at the age of 80.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **The stupa was built over a portion of Buddha's ashes and he was cremated by the ancient Malla tribes.**
 
• Ancient Buddhist texts reveal that the Ramabhar stupa has been referred to as Mukut-Bandhan Vihar.
 
• After getting enlightenment at Sarnath, Buddha shared four Noble Truths or Dharma.
 
 
• **The truth of suffering, the truth of the cause of suffering, the truth of the end of suffering, and the truth of the path that leads to the end of suffering.**

questions.question: Who among the following Indian singers received the ‘Bharat Ratna’ in 2001?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Lata Mangeshkar**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Bharat Ratna is India's highest civilian award** that is awarded for exceptional service in different categories including Literature, Art, Science, Public service, Sports or any field of human endeavour.

 
 
• It is given to a maximum of **3 person **in a** **particular year**.**
 
 
 
• **This award **is** first constituted** in the year** 1954** and the recommendations are made by the Prime Minister to the President, and no formal recommendations are needed.
 
• **C. Rajagopalachari was the first person to be honoured with Bharat Rarna, in 1954.**
 
• **Lata Mangeshkar** was an Indian singer who was considered one of the greatest singers of all time and recorded nearly 50,000 songs in 14 languages. 
 
 
• **She received the Bharat Ratna in 2001. Hence option 4 is correct.**
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **According to article 18 (1) of the Constitution, the award cannot be used as a prefix or suffix to the recipient's name but may be added to their biodata. **
 
• **Asha Bhosle** is an Indian playback singer who sang around 11,000 songs in 20 languages.
 
 
• ​She has won seven Filmfare Best Female Playback Awards and **in 2001, she received the Filmfare Lifetime achievement award.**
 
 
 
• **Shreya Ghoshal** is an Indian singer who predominantly sings in Hindi films and sang over 2000 songs in many languages.
 
 
• ​**She has won 4 National Awards for best female playback, and 7 Filmfare awards.**

questions.question: The minimum temperature of the day occurs generally ______.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**in the early morning**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The difference between high and low temperatures on the same day is called Diurnal temperature variation.
 
• **During the day, the air temperature increases as energy gains exceed the energy lost from Earth’s surface and during the night, the air temperature decreases as Earth’s surface loses more energy than it receives.**
 
• **The minimum temperature of the day usually occurs in the morning. Hence option 4 is correct. **
 
 
• **The maximum temperature occurs in the afternoon.**
 
 
 
• The average temperature on the Earth will be around 14ºC.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• Andaman and Nicobar islands are located near the equator and so they receive day and night equally throughout the year.
 
• **Near the equator, the sun’s rays are nearly perpendicular and concentrated over a smaller surface area causing warmer temperatures.**
 
• Both the Arctic (North Pole) and the Antarctic (South Pole) are very cold because they do not get much direct sunlight.

questions.question: Which scheme was launched in February 2022 to provide welfare and rehabilitation to the transgender community and the people engaged in the act of begging?

• There are 2 sub-schemes under this - ‘Central Sector Scheme for Comprehensive Rehabilitation for Welfare of Transgender Persons’ and ‘Central Sector Scheme for Comprehensive Rehabilitation of persons **engaged in the act of Begging’.**
 
• ​This umbrella scheme is designed to provide welfare measures to the Transgender community and the people engaged in the act of begging.

** [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] Additional Information__**

• Rural households are told not to dispose of garbage on the streets and instead hand it over to the** garbage collector.**
 
 
 
• **PM-DevINE** will be implemented by the Ministry of DoNER through the North Eastern Council or Central Ministries/ agencies.
 
 
• Measures would be taken to ensure adequate operation and maintenance of the projects sanctioned under PM-DevINE so that they are sustainable.

questions.question: Adityanath Yogi won from which constituency in the 2022 assembly elections?

questions.question: In the 18th century, the British fought ______ wars with the Mysore rulers.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Four**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

 
• The series of four wars fought between the British and the Kingdom of Mysore in South India during the 18th century was known as the Anglo-Mysore War.
 
 
• First Anglo-Mysore War: It was fought between 1767-1769 AD.

 
 
• Governor: Lord Verelst was the governor during this period.
 
• In the first Anglo-Mysore, the British, the Nizam, and the Marathas fought together against Hyder Ali.
 
• Treaty of Madras: Hyder Ali wins against the British. A defence treaty was concluded in 1769.
 
 
 
• Second Anglo-Mysore War: It was fought between 1780-1784 AD.
 
 
• Governor: Lord Warren Hastings was the governor during this period.
 
• In the second Anglo-Mysore, Hyder Ali, the Nizam, and the Marathas fought together against the British.
 
• Hyder Ali defeated Colonel Bailey.
 
• Hyder Ali died in 1782 during the Second Anglo-Mysore War and was succeeded by his son Tipu Sultan.
 
• Treaty of Mangalore: The Second Anglo-Mysore War ended with the signing of the Treaty of Mangalore by the Tipu Sultan in 1784.
 
 
 
• Third Anglo-Mysore War: It was fought between 1790-1792 AD.
 
 
• Governor: Lord Cornwallis was the governor during this period.
 
• In the third Anglo-Mysore, the British, the Nizam, and the Marathas fought together against Tipu Sultan.
 
• Treaty of Srirangapatna: It was signed by the Tipu Sultan in 1792.
 
 
 
• Fourth Anglo-Mysore War: It was fought in 1799.
 
 
• Governor: **Lord Wellesley** was the governor during this period.
 
• Tipu **died in 1799** while defending the Mysore capital, Srirangapatna.
 
• The threat of the French to the British ended by the year 1799.

questions.question: Sam has an income of ₹ 9 lacs per annum. Which tax slab (new regime) of India is applicable to him for FY 22-23?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**15%.**__ [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• Sam has an income of ₹ 9 lacs per annum.
 
• **15% tax slab **(new regime) of India is applicable to him for FY 22-23

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/db484db7c894cc40ce86af6865e8f373b25f0d417efd7756f8fc502c7466faa7.png] 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• According to the** Income Tax Act of India**, income tax is levied on all individuals, HUFs, partnership firms, LLPs, and corporations.
 
• If an individual's income exceeds the minimum threshold limit, they are subject to a slab system of taxation (known as the basic exemption limit).
 
• **Income Tax Slab:**
 
 
• Individual taxpayers in India pay income tax according to a slab system.
 
• Different tax rates are prescribed for different ranges of income under a slab system.
 
• It means that if a taxpayer's income rises, his or her tax rate rises as well.
 
• This sort of taxation helps the government to have progressive and equitable tax systems.
 
 
 
• The **rates for Tax slabs** are subject to change during every budget.

questions.question: Which of the following pairs of ‘Natural source-Acid’ is NOT correctly matched?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is **__Tamarind-Oxalic acid.__** [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• Vinegar: Acetic acid (it is present in nature organically and it can also be synthesized in the laboratory.
 
• Milk, Curd: Lactic acid (Converting milk into curd gives lactic acid naturally)
 
• Lemon, Orange: Citric acid. (Lemon is a natural source of Citric acid)
 
• **Oxalic acid** is an organic compound found in many plants, including leafy greens, vegetables, fruits, cocoa, nuts, and seeds.
 
 
• **Hence Tamarind-Oxalic acid is NOT correctly matched**.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Apple**: Malic acid ( Malic acid is present in apples, which is directly consumed by eating apples).
 
• **Tamarind, Grapes**: Tartaric acid. (Tamarind, Grapes are the organic natural source of tartaric acid)
 
• **Tomato**: Oxalic acid (Tomato is an organic natural source of Oxalic acid)

questions.question: Which type of unemployment is mostly found in urban areas?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is **__Educated unemployment.__** [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• Educated unemployment is mostly found in urban areas.
 
• When educated people do not find jobs it is called educated unemployment.
 
• Unemployment is a stage where an individual is willing and search for employment but fails to do so.
 
• The agriculture sector of India employs more than 50% of the total population and contributes around 16% to the GDP.​

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• Seasonal unemployment takes place when people are unemployed during a particular season or time of the year when labour demand is lesser than usual.
 
 
• The agriculture sector suffers from it because of the seasonal nature of crops and farming seasons. Hence 1 is correct.
 
 
 
• Disguised unemployment occurs when more people are employed than actually required.
 
 
• The marginal productivity of labour is zero. In agriculture, more people work in the field, and the same amount of work can be finished with a smaller workforce. 
 
 
 
• Frictional unemployment occurs when a person is unemployed by his choice and he is seeking a better job opportunity.
 
 
• It is good for the economy as the worker is looking for a job where he can be more productive.
 
 
 
• Open unemployment is the situation when a person is willing to work, is educated but is unable to get a job and work.
 
 
• This kind of unemployment is clearly visible in the society.

questions.question: Who, with the help of Kautilya, overthrew Dhanananda, the last Nanda ruler, in 322 BC?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is **__Chandragupta Maurya.__** [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Chandragupta Maurya** with the help of Kautilya, overthrew Dhanananda, the last Nanda ruler, in 322 BC.
 
• Chandragupta Maurya was the founder of the **Mauryan Empire.**
 
• He, at the young age of **25**, captured **Pataliputra **from the last ruler of the Nanda dynasty, Dhanananda. In this task, he was assisted by Kautilya, who was also known as Chanakya or Vishnugupta.
 
• Located on the hills of Kaimur, the city of **Pavapuri**, also known as Paava, is located near Rajgir and Bodh Gaya in Nalanda district of Bihar.
 
• This holy city for the followers of **Jainism**.
 
• Along with being the birthplace of Lord Mahavira, Vaishali is a city built out of Muzaffarpur Bihar. The main language here is Vajjika.
 
• Kushinagar, a city known as the Parinirvana Sthal of Mahatma Buddha, is located in the eastern frontier of Uttar Pradesh, whose former name is Kasia Bazaar.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Ashoka **the Great belonged to the Maurya Dynasty.

 
 
• The great ruler Ashoka ruled between 273 – 232 BC.
 
• This dynasty was formed by Chandragupta Maurya, in the present-day Bihar, after Defeating the Nanda dynasty ruler-Dhanananda.
 
 
 
• The full name of **Akbar **is "Abul-Fath Jala-ud-din Muhammad Akbar".
 
 
• He was born on **15 October 1542**.
 
• He was the third Mughal emperor.
 
• He got the title **"Akbar - The Great".**
 
• The Mansabdari administrative system was introduced by Akbar.
 
 
 
• **Kalashoka **is also called **Kakavarna**.
 
 
• Kalashok became the successor of Shishunaga and the ruler of Magadha.
 
• After Shishunag, his son Kalashok died in 394 BC. He ascended the throne and ruled for about 28 years.
 
• Kalashok made Pataliputra his capital instead of **Vaishali**.

questions.question: Which of the following airports is located in Amritsar?

options.text: Sri Guru Ram Das Ji International Airport

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

• The airport is** Punjab's biggest and busiest airport.**

• In India, the airport experienced the** third-fastest growth during the 2017–18 fiscal year.**

• **Dr Babasaheb Ambedkar International Airport:**
 
 
• An international airport serving **Nagpur, Maharashtra, **India is Dr Babasaheb Ambedkar International Airport.
 
• It was given the** B. R. Ambedkar name in 2005.**
 
 
 
• **Indira Gandhi International Airport:**
 
 
• The** main international airport serving Delhi **is Indira Gandhi International Airport.

questions.question: Push and pull factors are associated with which component of the population?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Migration.**__ [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **International migration** is the outcome of a** mix of forces that push people** away from their countries of origin and** entice them t**o a particular destination country.
 
• **Push factors **can include
 
 
• **armed conflict, **
 
• **natural disasters,**
 
• the lack of** job opportunities,**
 
• the possession of** economic and cultural capital,**
 
• a family **break up** or
 
• **dissatisfaction** with one’s own life and surroundings
 
 
 
• **Pull factors** can often be the polar opposites of the push factors, i.e.
 
 
• **greater security,**
 
• better** job opportunities** or
 
• the prospect of a more **exciting life.**
 
 
 
• However, some pull factors, such as closeness to a **push factor or the presence of family or community members **in the destination nation, do not immediately correlate with push factors.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Death rate:**

 
 
• A** population's mortality rate **is often known as death rate.
 
• It is a measurement of the **number of deaths** within that** population per unit of time**, scaled to that population's size.
 
 
 
• **Birth rate:**
 
 
• The number of babies born in a population in a specific period of time is known as the birth rate.

questions.question: Who among the following was the first to bring the concept of modern dance to India with his novel approach and works?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is__** Uday Shankar.**__ [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• Uday Shankar was an **Indian dancer and choreographer.**
 
• He is well renowned for** infusing elements **of **Indian classical, folk, and tribal dance** into a fusion style of dance by adopting **European theatrical techniques** to Indian classical dance.
 
• He received a **Sangeet Natak Akademi award** in** 1962.**
 
• The Indian government gave him the **Padma Vibhushan**, its second-highest civilian honor, in** 1971.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Guru Bipin Singh: **

 
 
• Guru Bipin Singh was a** manipuri dance director, choreographer, and instructor.**
 
• **In 1966**, he received the **Sangeet Natak Akademi Prize.**
 
 
 
• **Padma Subrahmanyam:**
 
 
• Padma Subrahmanyam, is an** Indian classical Bharata Natyam dancer.**
 
• She was awarded with **Sangeet Natak Akademi Award (1983), Padma Bhushan (2003), and Padma Shri (1981).**
 
 
 
• **Kelucharan Mohapatra:**
 
 
• Kelucharan Mohapatra was a **well-known guru, performer, and exponent** of Indian classical dance.
 
• In the 20th century, he is credited with bringing back and popularizing this** classical dancing style.**
 
• He is the first recipient of the** Padma Vibhushan award from Odisha.**
